correctness.rationale: The cavity equation yields the exact q-regular tree free Green kernel g(z)h(z)^distance and finite edge limit c*r^distance. Strictly negative derivative of the compressed resolvent gives exactly one above-band crossing per supercritical edge eigenvalue and none at equality. A tridiagonal inverse of the geometric Toeplitz kernel yields simple angular roots and ordered finite-p thresholds. Toeplitz Fourier bounds and endpoint angular expansions yield exact cooperative thresholds and the two p^-2 shifts; root equidistribution yields the piecewise arccosine per-impurity density. The embedded reproducibility script passes 1437 independent numerical comparisons; finite balls are only approximations, not infinite-volume proof.

value.rationale: The natural gap is whether a line of individually subcritical positive lattice defects can nevertheless create bound states on a nonamenable tree, where unlike in the 2D square lattice no arbitrarily weak single impurity binds. The theorem gives exact all-finite-array thresholds, the cooperative-onset/saturation interval, sharp inverse-square finite-size corrections, and a computable limiting proportion of modes. These provide a complete physically relevant design classification beyond a generic implicit Green determinant; no general new determinant or Toeplitz theorem is claimed.
